title: Economic Evaluation of the Nitrate Sensitive Areas Scheme - ER02019
description: This document describes an evaluation of the UK's Nitrate Sensitive Areas Scheme (NSA Scheme), which aims to reduce nitrate pollution from agricultural practices. The scheme encourages farmers to adopt environmentally friendly land management options, such as converting arable land to grassland and reducing fertilizer use. The evaluation, conducted by ENTEC for the Ministry of Agriculture, Fisheries & Food, utilized surveys and data analysis to examine the scheme's impact on farming practices, nitrogen application, farm incomes, and participant attitudes. Results show that the scheme has led to significant changes in farming practices, with a general reduction in inorganic nitrogen use and some changes in crop outputs. Participants were willing to adapt to the scheme's requirements, which resulted in economic impacts, including changes in farm incomes and cost savings. The scheme also increased livestock outputs and led to an average income increase of £45 per hectare for participants. However, the flexibility of the scheme allowed for intensification on ineligible land, which may limit its overall effectiveness. Recommendations for scheme improvements include adjusting payment levels, enhancing incentives, and providing more feedback to participants on the environmental impact of their practices.

title: Economic evaluation of Set Aside
description: This document describes an evaluation of the European Union's set-aside policies, which were implemented to reduce surplus cereal production and enhance environmental benefits. The evaluation employed a range of methods, including surveys, stakeholder input, and environmental impact reviews, to assess the policy's effectiveness. Results indicate that while set-aside policies have successfully reduced cereal production and provided habitats for wildlife, they have also led to economic inefficiencies and conflicting objectives. The study suggests that spatial targeting could improve outcomes, and that direct price support removal might be a more efficient solution to oversupply. The policy has had a mixed impact on UK agriculture and wildlife, with some environmental benefits but variable outcomes depending on management practices. It has also affected farm profitability and technical efficiency, with larger farms experiencing greater reductions in gross margin. The evaluation concludes that set-aside policies have had mixed effectiveness, with environmental and agricultural benefits but also unintended economic consequences. Alternative policy scenarios, including voluntary and competitive set-aside schemes, are discussed as potentially more cost-effective options. The document recommends considering alternative supply control mechanisms and integrating environmental objectives for greater policy effectiveness.

title: Evaluation of the effectiveness of the Waterfringe Option Scheme on environmental quality
file_title: Evaluation of the Effectiveness of the Water Fringe Option Scheme on Environmental Quality
description: This document describes an evaluation of the Water Fringe Option Scheme (WFOS) and other agri-environment schemes in England, such as the Countryside Stewardship Scheme (CSS), Environmentally Sensitive Areas (ESAs), Wildlife Enhancement Scheme (WES), and Nitrate Sensitive Areas (NSAs). These programs are designed to encourage farmers to adopt practices that protect and enhance water quality and wildlife habitats. The evaluation, conducted by RPS Clouston for the Environment Agency, employed literature reviews, consultations, field visits, monitoring studies, and environmental reports to determine the effectiveness of these schemes. Findings suggest that while the WFOS shows promise for water quality and habitat improvement, broader land changes are necessary for significant environmental gains. Schemes like CSS and ESA have had a positive impact on biodiversity and landscape, but further monitoring is needed to verify certain benefits, such as the impact of grassland management on water quality. The evaluation concludes that these schemes contribute to environmental conservation but may not fully address all water quality issues. It recommends integrating successful elements of the WFOS into existing schemes and emphasizes the need for inter-agency collaboration to optimize land management for water environment protection.
